F1: The factory reuses the pool that strategy shutdown permanently closes, so recreated strategies cannot process submitted messages.
F2: Workers stop after their current item and the commit thread exits before later completions can be committed, abandoning accepted work during shutdown.
F3: Unbounded queues can accumulate work without limit, allowing ingestion to exhaust memory when processing falls behind.
F4: Worker and submission exceptions still mark offsets complete, allowing failed or unprocessed messages to be committed.
F5: The test may assert before the one-second commit cycle runs, and factory shutdown does not stop the strategy’s commit thread.
